_doc: Synthetic customer fixture for recommendation_eval.py. Each customer is a real DB row with real CustomerInteraction history. The eval is conformance against design claims (rec engine does what it claims), NOT ground-truth benchmarking. Do not infer customer-level preference from these labels.
claims_under_test: C8 (no duplicate product_id within rec set)

customers._note: Diverse history -- stresses diversity_floor without single-category collapse
Tests that adult-targeted recs surface for adult-self customers, not baby items.

customers.profile_label: gift buyer (variety across ages and product_types)
customers._note: Deliberately spans bib/playset/book/backpack/bodysuit/action_figure/pacifier across infant/toddler/kids/teen. Stresses persona-diffusion handling and diversity floor. Genuinely spread (no dominant age) -- the age_coherence guard must NOT fire here.

customers.profile_label: gift buyer skewed to older kids (age-coherence stress)
customers._note: Purchases concentrate on older-kid product_types restricted to kids/teen, so age_group has a clear center of mass. Adjacent infant items can still surface via shared use_case/product_type + boosters. Stresses PersonaCoherenceDemoter / the age_coherence check: top-N must not collapse onto infant. This is the gift_buyer cross-age collapse both rubric reviewers flagged.
1 purchase -- triggers cold_start (interaction_count < 3). Tests C6 (cold_start flag) and C24 (still returns recs with damped scores).
Recent purchases include diapers, bibs, etc. Tests C10 (one-time products dropped) and C11 (repurchasable within window dropped). Saturation pattern stress.
